#2064. PSG transfer news: Paris ready to open door to January departure

By Axel Clody | 20 Nov 2026 06:29

Lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain in the next winter transfer window. The Parisian club are ready to let him go on one condition.

Having joined PSG in the summer of 2025 from Lille for £34m (€40m), Lucas Chevalier has failed to make his mark at the Parisian club. While he was expected to succeed Gianluigi Donnarumma, he now finds himself as a mere understudy to Matvey Safonov.

The Russian goalkeeper has won his place as first choice and is not letting go of it. Paris are very pleased with his performances and have reportedly even secretly wrapped up a contract extension. Safonov has played every game for the two-time European champions this season, leaving Lucas Chevalier without any game time.

It is a difficult situation for the French international, who missed the last World Cup and has not been called up by new France manager Zinedine Zidane.

Already mentioned as a possible departure last summer, the former Lille man had chosen to stay. Canal+ reports that PSG had told him he would get a fresh chance if he kept working.

However, that chance never came. A point of no return appears to have been reached. ‘He wants to play, he needs to play. Today, his wish is to look elsewhere to find game time’ - Gauthier Kuntzmann revealed on the Late Football Club show. The Parisian club are ready to let him leave this winter.

‘Paris Saint-Germain are aware that the situation of Lucas Chevalier cannot drag on. On top of that, he is losing market value and that is a factor, even if everything is going very well financially at PSG. 'I am telling you, Paris Saint-Germain do not rule out the idea, even in the short term, of seeing Lucas Chevalier leave on loan or in a sale, it will depend on the offers’ - Philippe Carayon explained on the same show.

The task does not look simple for Lucas Chevalier. ‘Finding a goalkeeper position at a good club in January will not be simple. Except in the event of an injury at a club’ - Alain Roche warned. In any case, in this saga, PSG will only let their goalkeeper leave on one condition.

‘There will be an absolute prerequisite for Paris Saint-Germain, which is to find a top-level replacement for Safonov’ - Philippe Carayon stressed. That could complicate a departure for the French goalkeeper in January 2027 even further.

#2063. Oliver Glasner has no choice but to axe Nottingham Forest player who lost 11 out of 12 duels vs Bournemouth

Correspondent AUTHORITY NCTJ-qualified football journalist with experience at VAVEL, Hayters TV, SPORTbible, and Centredevils. FOCUS Premier League analysis, tactical deep-dives, and original opinion content across Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester City, and Celtic. THE INSIGHT Evan utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, high-speed reporting. He provides specialist tactical and analytical content to ensure fans get beyond the headlines and understand the full picture.

Dan Ndoye was utterly dismal as Nottingham Forest were beaten 2-0 by Bournemouth on Saturday.

Evanilson and Justin Kluivert scored for the home side, who ultimately could have added one or two more on the day.

The visitors looked to come back into it in the second half but failed to find a way through, and have seen their momentum halted.

Nottingham Forest broken their duck under Oliver Glasner by winning just their second Premier League game of the season, against Manchester City just before the break.

But the Austrian will now have to return to the drawing board, and one of his first decisions will have to involve Ndoye.

The 26-year-old, who arrived last year for around £34million, is still yet to really find his feet in the Premier League.

Ndoye would only last 45 minutes before he was hooked by Glasner, such was his display appalling.

The winger failed to leave any impact, and was practically invisible as Nottingham Forest struggled to create.

He misplaced four of his 11 attempted passes, with not a single one of them resulting in a chance for his teammates.

Ndoye's only actual shot was blocked, and he made only two passes into the final third.

But it gets even worse. The 26-year-old was dispossessed twice and dribbled past once, giving away three fouls and not earning any himself.

Most shockingly of all, Ndoye would win just two of the 12 duels he contested against Bournemouth before he was hauled off.

In search of a better second half, Glasner brought on Igor Jesus for Ndoye, and the difference was immediate.

In his 45 minutes, the Brazilian created a chance, took five shots ad won four duels.

And as a team, Nottingham Forest took four more shots, created 1.27 more expected goals and doubled their touches in the opposition box.

It begs the question about why Jesus did not start the game, even when Ndoye has been for some time now.

Saturday's game should serve as a learning moment for Glasner, who can really not afford to have too many more.
